# Echoes — a gossip simulation

Echoes is a browser RPG where a single AI-generated image becomes a living village you walk through. Every villager is its own agent — one LLM (GPT‑4o) voiced through per-character personas, moods, and secrets, so each sounds like a distinct person, not a menu. The heart of it is a gossip simulation: rumors start from one source, spread mouth-to-mouth as villagers gather and talk, and every hop is traced into a live memory graph persisted to Supermemory. You can plant your own rumors and watch them travel. It's a small, legible sandbox for studying how information — and misinformation — propagates through a community.

![A generated village populated by LLM-voiced agents, gathering in the square where news spreads](docs/village.png)

> The village of *Hollow Waystead*. Villagers gather in the square — that's where rumors jump from one person to a whole crowd. Press **M** for the live gossip graph:

![The community memory graph — every rumor traced from its single origin](docs/gossip-graph.png)

## What's inside

- **One generated world.** Type a theme and the whole arena is generated as a single top-down image (fal.ai FLUX), populated with small wandering villagers.
- **Agents, not scripts.** Every NPC is voiced by GPT‑4o through its own system prompt — personality, mood, current activity, a private want and a secret, plus a stable per-character speech quirk. Two villagers never answer the same line the same way.
- **A gossip engine with provenance.** Each rumor has a single origin villager. When two idle villagers meet, whoever holds fresh news tells everyone in the huddle. Every "A told B" hop is recorded, so any rumor traces back to its source as a spreading tree.
- **Player-planted rumors.** In conversation, `send` is private; **🗣 rumor** plants what you say — you become its origin and it spreads from there.
- **Fresh news over time.** The village starts near-silent (2–3 rumors); new ones are coined as play continues, so gossip never fully dries up.
- **A live memory graph.** Persisted to Supermemory as one shared per-world container.

## Controls

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| WASD / arrows · scroll | move · zoom |
| click or **E** | talk to a villager |
| **🗣 rumor** (in chat) | plant a rumor — you become its source |
| **M** | live community memory graph + per-rumor thread tracer |
| **P** | persona roster of the whole population |

## Running locally

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local   # then fill in your keys
npm run dev                  # http://localhost:3000
```

Keys (see `.env.example`):

- `FAL_KEY` — fal.ai, for the world background and NPC portraits.
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` — GPT‑4o, for NPC dialogue. (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` works as an alternative — Claude.)
- `SUPERMEMORY_API_KEY` — optional; persists the gossip graph across sessions.

Without a dialogue key, NPCs fall back to a scripted engine; without `FAL_KEY`, a procedural placeholder world is drawn. The app runs either way.

## How it works

- **World** — a single bounded arena generated as one image; villagers wander, gather at a shared square, and mix so rumors travel the whole map.
- **Dialogue** — one stateless GPT‑4o call per NPC turn, scoped to only that character's persona, memory, and known rumors. Same model, different masks.
- **Gossip** — a deterministic simulation (movement, meeting, spread) in `lib/engine.ts` and `lib/agents.ts`; the LLM handles voice, the code handles who-knows-what and how it travels.
- **Memory** — each hop and each NPC memory is written to Supermemory; the community graph is drawn from the in-engine ledger, live.

Built with Next.js 14, TypeScript, and a hand-drawn canvas renderer.
